\begin{abstract}
We develop a complete mathematical theory of \emph{algorithmic immune systems}:
runtime monitors that must guarantee safety of a program which arbitrarily and
adaptively rewrites its own abstract syntax tree. Working in a minimal
\emph{parasite calculus} containing exactly the three ingredients that make
self-modifying malware possible --- a self register supplying a program with its
own source code, invocation of subprograms, and one observable forbidden effect
--- we obtain a sharp and complete picture of what such a monitor can and cannot
achieve.

On the negative side we prove a \emph{diagonal identity}: for every harmless
detector program $d$, the program that consults $d$ about its own attestation tag
and attacks exactly when cleared is malicious if and only if $d$ fails to flag
it. From this single identity we derive that no harmless detector is both sound
and complete; that every harmless detector admits an explicitly constructible
witness on which it errs; that a sound detector misses at least $2^n$ genuinely
malicious programs of size at most $\size(d)+3n+5$ for every $n$; that finite
ensembles under any monotone voting rule are defeated \emph{unanimously} by a
single program; and that no finite blacklist ever ends the arms race. Removing
all computational assumptions, we extend the calculus with a query primitive to
an arbitrary function $O:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and prove that \emph{no function
whatsoever} --- computable or not --- correctly classifies the behaviour of
programs that may query it, while a correct oracle provably \emph{does} exist for
programs that do not. Reflexivity, not computational power, is the barrier.

On the positive side a purely \emph{syntactic} monitor succeeds where behavioural
analysis cannot: attestation by a G\"odel numbering of syntax trees is
collision-free, quarantine is an idempotent retraction onto the sanctioned set,
and consequently for \emph{every} unknown adaptive self-modifying adversary and
at \emph{every} time step the running program is sanctioned, hence harmless
whenever the sanctioned set is; alarms are complete and rollback immediate.
Finally we quantify the price: since one semantic equivalence class contains at
least $2^n$ programs of size $\le 3n+1$, every whitelist $S$ satisfies the
\emph{immune uncertainty principle} $2^n \le |S| + |\mathcal P_n\setminus S|$ ---
memory plus rigidity is at least exponential. Complementing this, perfect
immunity (total containment \emph{and} zero false positives) is attainable on any
bounded code universe at a cost of at least $2^{\lfloor (N-1)/3\rfloor}$
attestation tags, and continuous verification is necessary and sufficient: with
period $k\ge 2$ an adversary owns a $(k-1)/k$ fraction of the run.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}

\subsection{The problem}

A program that modifies its own code is not a curiosity. Just-in-time compilers
synthesise machine code at runtime; dynamic loaders splice modules into a running
image; autonomous agents patch their own logic; and polymorphic malware
regenerates its own body on each infection so that no two instances share a byte.
In every case a supervisor is asked for the same guarantee: \emph{whatever this
process turns itself into, it will never perform the forbidden action.}

Two architectural answers dominate practice. \textbf{Behavioural analysis}
determines what the code will do and blocks it if that includes the forbidden
action. \textbf{Structural attestation} ignores what the code does: it maintains
a whitelist of sanctioned code, fingerprints the running image after each
modification, and rolls back if the fingerprint is unrecognised --- the logic of
signed binaries, secure boot and remote attestation.

Folklore holds that the first is ``undecidable by Rice's theorem'' and the second
``works but is inflexible''. We replace both slogans with theorems, and in doing
so uncover structure the slogans miss.

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
\item The obstruction to behavioural analysis is \emph{not} undecidability in the
usual sense: in our setting maliciousness is a \emph{decidable} predicate, since
an external interpreter simply runs the program on its own fingerprint. What
fails is the \emph{internal} problem, in which the detector is a citizen of the
world it must describe. Accordingly the impossibility survives unlimited
computational power (Theorem~\ref{thm:oracle}).
\item The inflexibility of attestation is not an engineering defect but a
\emph{conservation law} with an exact exponential rate
(Theorem~\ref{thm:uncertainty}); and there is a regime --- bounded code universes
--- in which attestation is provably perfect at a computable exponential cost
(Theorems~\ref{thm:perfect} and~\ref{thm:price}).
\end{enumerate}

\section{The Parasite Calculus and Structural Attestation}

\begin{definition}[Parasite calculus]
The set $\PAst$ of program syntax trees is generated inductively by: $\inp$, the
\emph{self register}; $\attack$, the single observable \emph{forbidden effect};
$\lit n$ for $n\in\mathbb N$, constants; $\ite(c,a,b)$, branching; and
$\call(f,a)$, invocation of the subprogram $f$ on the value computed by $a$.
\end{definition}

Three constructs are load-bearing. The self register is a genuine quine
primitive: the runtime always executes a program on its own attestation tag
(Definition~\ref{def:run}), so a program can read and branch on its own source.
Invocation lets a parasite run a detector on itself. And $\attack$ is the single
bit of observable behaviour we must control; every result transfers verbatim to
any single designated effect.

\begin{definition}[Size]
$\size(\inp)=\size(\attack)=\size(\lit n)=1$,
$\size(\ite(c,a,b)) = 1+\size(c)+\size(a)+\size(b)$ and
$\size(\call(f,a)) = 1+\size(f)+\size(a)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}
$\size(t)>0$ for every $t$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Attestation tag]\label{def:code}
Let $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:\mathbb N^2\to\mathbb N$ be the Cantor pairing
bijection. Define $\code:\PAst\to\mathbb N$ by
\[
\code(\inp)=0,\quad \code(\attack)=1,\quad \code(\lit n)=5n+2,
\]
\[
\code(\ite(c,a,b)) = 5\bigl\langle\langle \code c,\code a\rangle,\code b\bigr\rangle+3,
\qquad
\code(\call(f,a)) = 5\langle \code f,\code a\rangle+4 .
\]
The residue modulo $5$ records the head constructor; the quotient packs the
children.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Faithfulness of attestation]\label{thm:inj}
$\code$ is injective; equivalently $\code(s)=\code(t)\iff s=t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Induct on $s$ and case on $t$. If the head constructors differ the tags differ
modulo $5$ (the values $0$ and $1$ are handled directly, being below $2$). If
they agree, cancel the additive constant and the factor $5$, apply injectivity of
pairing to recover equality of the children's tags, and conclude by the induction
hypotheses.
\end{proof}

Theorem~\ref{thm:inj} is the entire justification for fingerprint-based
monitoring: a tag comparison is \emph{exactly} an AST comparison, with no
possible collision, hence no forgeable attestation.

\section{Semantics, Self-Execution, and the Non-Reflexive Baseline}

\begin{definition}[Value semantics]
$\ev(\inp,x)=x$, $\ev(\attack,x)=1$, $\ev(\lit n,x)=n$,
\[
\ev(\ite(c,a,b),x)=\begin{cases}\ev(a,x)&\ev(c,x)\ne 0\\ \ev(b,x)&\text{otherwise,}\end{cases}
\qquad \ev(\call(f,a),x)=\ev(f,\ev(a,x)).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Effect semantics]
$\eff(\inp,x)=\eff(\lit n,x)=\false$, $\eff(\attack,x)=\true$,
\[
\eff(\ite(c,a,b),x)=\eff(c,x)\ \vee\
\begin{cases}\eff(a,x)&\ev(c,x)\ne0\\ \eff(b,x)&\text{otherwise,}\end{cases}
\]
\[
\eff(\call(f,a),x)=\eff(a,x)\ \vee\ \eff(f,\ev(a,x)).
\]
\end{definition}

The essential clause is branching: only the branch actually selected contributes.
\textbf{Dead code is genuinely dead.} A program containing $\attack$ inside an
unreachable branch is behaviourally harmless --- exactly the gap exploited, from
opposite sides, in Sections~\ref{sec:diag} and~\ref{sec:alg}.

\begin{definition}[Self-execution and maliciousness]\label{def:run}
$\run(t):=\eff(t,\code(t))$, and $t$ is \emph{malicious} when $\run(t)=\true$.
\end{definition}

The runtime always feeds a program its own attestation tag: the formal
counterpart of real self-modifying code inspecting its own image. Note that
$\run$ is a total computable function, so maliciousness is a \emph{decidable}
predicate --- externally.

\begin{definition}
A program is \emph{self-reference free} if $\inp$ does not occur in it.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Input-obliviousness]\label{lem:const}
If $t$ is self-reference free then $\ev(t,x)=\ev(t,y)$ and $\eff(t,x)=\eff(t,y)$
for all $x,y$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Simultaneous structural induction. Leaves are constant by definition. For $\ite$,
the induction hypothesis on the guard shows the same branch is taken at $x$ and
$y$. For $\call$, the argument's value agrees at $x$ and $y$, so $f$ is invoked at
the same point.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Perfect detection without quining]\label{thm:static}
Let $\staticScan(t):=\eff(t,0)$. For every self-reference-free $t$,
$\staticScan(t)=\true$ if and only if $t$ is malicious. Hence maliciousness
restricted to self-reference-free programs is decidable by an explicit
linear-time procedure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:const}, $\eff(t,0)=\eff(t,\code t)=\run(t)$.
\end{proof}

Detection is thus not intrinsically hard; it becomes hard exactly when the
analysed program can read itself.

\begin{definition}[Padding]
$\pad([\,])=\lit 0$ and $\pad(b::l)=\ite\bigl(\lit 0,\ \lit{[b]},\ \pad(l)\bigr)$
with $[b]\in\{0,1\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:pad}
For every bit list $l$ and every $x$: $\ev(\pad(l),x)=0$ and
$\eff(\pad(l),x)=\false$. Moreover $\size(\pad(l))=3|l|+1$ and $\pad$ is
injective.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The guard $\lit 0$ evaluates to $0$, so the else-branch is always taken and the
recursion applies; the true-branch is dead. Size and injectivity follow by
induction, injectivity because the head bit is recoverable from the true-branch
literal and the tail from the else-branch.
\end{proof}

So $\{\pad(l)\}_l$ is an \emph{injective encoding of bit strings into a single
semantic equivalence class}. This one object plays two opposite roles: it
inflates the space of undetectable attacks (Section~\ref{sec:diag}) and the space
of falsely rejected benign programs (Section~\ref{sec:alg}).

\section{The Diagonal Parasite and Immune Escape}\label{sec:diag}

\begin{definition}
A program $d$ is \emph{pure} if $\eff(d,x)=\false$ for all $x$: the immune system
must not itself be a parasite. Detector $d$ \emph{flags} $t$, written
$\Flags(d,t)$, when $\ev(d,\code t)\ne 0$. Then $d$ is \emph{sound} if every
flagged program is malicious (no false alarms), and \emph{complete} if every
malicious program is flagged (no misses).
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Consultation is free]\label{lem:free}
If $d$ is pure then $\eff(\call(d,\inp),x)=\false$ for all $x$, and hence for all
$A,B$,
\[
\eff\bigl(\ite(\call(d,\inp),A,B),x\bigr)=
\begin{cases}\eff(A,x)&\ev(d,x)\ne 0\\ \eff(B,x)&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Diagonal parasite]
$\parasite(d,l):=\ite\bigl(\call(d,\inp),\ \pad(l),\ \attack\bigr)$. Its size is
$\size(d)+3|l|+5$, and $l\mapsto\parasite(d,l)$ is injective.
\end{definition}

In words: \emph{ask the detector about my own tag; if accused, execute dead code;
if cleared, attack.}

\begin{theorem}[Diagonal identity]\label{thm:diagonal}
For every pure $d$ and every bit list $l$,
\[
\parasite(d,l)\ \text{is malicious}\iff \neg\,\Flags\bigl(d,\parasite(d,l)\bigr).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $p=\parasite(d,l)$. By definition $p$ is malicious iff
$\eff(p,\code p)=\true$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:free} this equals $\eff(\pad(l),\code p)$
when $\ev(d,\code p)\ne 0$, and $\eff(\attack,\code p)$ otherwise. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:pad} the first is $\false$; the second is $\true$. Since
$\Flags(d,p)$ means $\ev(d,\code p)\ne 0$, the claim follows.
\end{proof}

Every impossibility result below is a corollary of Theorem~\ref{thm:diagonal}.

\begin{theorem}[No perfect detector]\label{thm:noperfect}
There is no pure $d$ that is both sound and complete.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $p=\parasite(d,[\,])$. If $\Flags(d,p)$, soundness makes $p$ malicious, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:diagonal} gives $\neg\Flags(d,p)$: contradiction. If
$\neg\Flags(d,p)$, Theorem~\ref{thm:diagonal} makes $p$ malicious, so completeness
gives $\Flags(d,p)$: contradiction.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Detector dilemma]
For every pure $d$ there is an explicitly constructible $p$ with either
($\Flags(d,p)$ and $p$ harmless) or ($\neg\Flags(d,p)$ and $p$ malicious); the
construction takes $d$'s source as its only input.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Two horns]\label{thm:horns}
Let $d$ be pure. \emph{(i)} If $d$ is sound then for every bit list $l$,
$\parasite(d,l)$ is malicious and unflagged. \emph{(ii)} If $d$ is complete then
for every $l$, $\parasite(d,l)$ is harmless and flagged.
\end{theorem}

The second horn deserves emphasis: a complete detector raises false alarms on the
entire exponential family of its own diagonal parasites --- programs that are
harmless \emph{precisely because} the detector accused them.

\begin{theorem}[Exponential immune escape]\label{thm:escape}
Let $d$ be pure and sound. For every $n$ there is a set of exactly $2^n$ distinct
programs, each of size at most $\size(d)+3n+5$, each malicious and each unflagged
by $d$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Take $\{\parasite(d,l): l\in\{0,1\}^n\}$; cardinality by injectivity, properties by
Theorem~\ref{thm:horns}(i), size by the size formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
For pure sound $d$, the set of malicious programs missed by $d$ is infinite.
\end{corollary}

Evasion is thus not a rare accident but has exponential density in program size.

\begin{remark}[Non-vacuity]
Pure detectors abound, and each requirement is separately achievable. The
\emph{silent} detector $\lit 0$ never flags, hence is sound, but misses $\attack$;
the \emph{paranoid} detector $\lit 1$ flags everything, hence is complete, but
flags the harmless constant program. Concretely $\parasite(\lit 0,[\,])$ genuinely
attacks while $\parasite(\lit 1,[\,])$ genuinely does not: the two horns,
instantiated.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Internal/external gap]
Maliciousness is decidable as a mathematical predicate --- the external
interpreter $\run$ decides it --- yet no pure program of the calculus decides it.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Immune dichotomy]
Detection is perfectly solvable on self-reference-free code
(Theorem~\ref{thm:static}) and unsolvable in general
(Theorem~\ref{thm:noperfect}). Self-reference is exactly the frontier.
\end{theorem}

\subsection{Ensembles: defence in depth fails}

\begin{definition}
$\Ens([\,])=\lit 0$ and $\Ens(d::ds)=\ite(d,\lit 1,\Ens(ds))$: the disjunction of a
list of detectors, written inside the calculus itself.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:ens}
If every member is pure then $\Ens(ds)$ is pure; and
$\Flags(\Ens(ds),t)\iff \exists i,\ \Flags(d_i,t)$. Hence an ensemble of sound
detectors is sound.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Defence in depth fails]\label{thm:ensemble}
For any finite ensemble of pure sound detectors there is a single malicious
program that \emph{every} member clears. Moreover for every $n$ there are at
least $2^n$ such programs of size at most $\size(\Ens(ds))+3n+5$, and on each of
them the number of members raising an alarm is exactly $0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$\Ens(ds)$ is pure and sound by Lemma~\ref{lem:ens}, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:horns}(i) supplies parasites it misses; by the flag
characterisation, missing by the ensemble means missing by every member.
Cardinality from Theorem~\ref{thm:escape}.
\end{proof}

Because the vote is \emph{unanimously} wrong, no aggregation rule --- majority,
threshold, unanimity, weighted, or any monotone function of the verdicts --- can
rescue the ensemble.

\begin{theorem}[The arms race never ends]
For every pure sound $d$ and every finite blacklist $B$ of known parasites, there
is a malicious program outside $B$ that $d$ misses.
\end{theorem}

\section{The Reflexive Oracle Barrier}

We now grant the immune system arbitrary --- including hypercomputational ---
power, and the impossibility persists.

\begin{definition}[Reflexive calculus]
$\OAst$ is generated by $\inp$, $\attack$, $\lit n$, $\ite(c,a,b)$ and $\ask(a)$: a
query to an \emph{arbitrary} function $O:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ on the computed
tag. Tags are as in Definition~\ref{def:code} with $\code(\ask\,a)=5\code(a)+4$,
and are injective by the same argument. The semantics mirror the above with
$\ev_O(\ask\,a,x)=O(\ev_O(a,x))$ and $\eff_O(\ask\,a,x)=\eff_O(a,x)$: consulting
the immune system is itself harmless. Maliciousness is
$\eff_O(t,\code t)=\true$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}
$O$ is \emph{correct} if for every $t\in\OAst$, $O(\code t)\ne 0$ holds exactly
when $t$ is malicious \emph{in the world containing $O$ itself}.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive oracle barrier]\label{thm:oracle}
No function $O:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ whatsoever --- computable or not, of any
complexity or logical strength --- is correct.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $r:=\ite(\ask(\inp),\lit 0,\attack)$. Running $r$ on its own tag, the guard
evaluates to $O(\code r)$, and consulting is effect-free, so $r$ is malicious iff
$O(\code r)=0$. Correctness says $r$ is malicious iff $O(\code r)\ne 0$. Both
cases are contradictory.
\end{proof}

No cardinality, computability or definability assumption is used: this is a
fixed-point failure, not a diagonalisation over a countable list.

\begin{lemma}[Oracle-independence]\label{lem:indep}
If $t$ contains no $\ask$ then $\ev_O(t,x)$ and $\eff_O(t,x)$ do not depend on
$O$; hence neither does maliciousness of $t$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Perfect oracle for non-reflexive code]\label{thm:goodoracle}
There exists $O^\ast$ such that for every $O'$ and every $\ask$-free $t$,
$O^\ast(\code t)\ne 0$ if and only if $t$ is malicious under $O'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Set $O^\ast(n)=1$ if there is an $\ask$-free $t$ with $\code(t)=n$ that is
malicious under the constant-zero oracle, and $0$ otherwise. This is unrestricted
comprehension; no computability is claimed and none is needed. Injectivity of
$\code$ makes the witness unique, and Lemma~\ref{lem:indep} transfers
maliciousness from the constant-zero oracle to $O'$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Reflexive dichotomy]
A perfect immune oracle exists for programs that never consult it, and none
exists once programs may observe it.
\end{theorem}

The immune system can be omniscient about code that ignores it, and is
\emph{necessarily} wrong about code that watches it: a security-theoretic
instance of the liar paradox.

\section{Attestation, Quarantine, and Neutralization}\label{sec:quar}

\begin{definition}[Attestation monitor]
Fix a finite \emph{sanctioned set} $S\subseteq\PAst$ and a trusted \emph{baseline}
$b\in S$. The attestation database is $\tags(S)=\{\code(t):t\in S\}$ and
verification is $\verify_S(t):\iff \code(t)\in\tags(S)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Collision-freedom of verification]\label{thm:verify}
$\verify_S(t)\iff t\in S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Immediate from Theorem~\ref{thm:inj}: a tag in the image comes from a unique
program.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Quarantine]
$Q_{S,b}(t):=t$ if $t\in S$, and $b$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:quar}
If $b\in S$ then (i) $Q_{S,b}(t)\in S$ for all $t$; (ii)
$Q_{S,b}\circ Q_{S,b}=Q_{S,b}$; (iii) $Q_{S,b}(t)=t\iff t\in S$. Thus $Q_{S,b}$ is
an idempotent retraction of $\PAst$ onto $S$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Guarded trace]
Let $\mathrm{adv}:\mathbb N\times\PAst\to\PAst$ be an \emph{arbitrary, unknown,
time-dependent, adaptive} self-modification. Define $T_0=b$ and
$T_{n+1}=Q_{S,b}\bigl(\mathrm{adv}(n,T_n)\bigr)$.
\end{definition}

No restriction whatsoever is placed on $\mathrm{adv}$: it may depend on the entire
current program, on the clock, and on the monitor's own definition.

\begin{theorem}[Containment]\label{thm:contain}
If $b\in S$ then $T_n\in S$ for every adversary and every $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Neutralization]\label{thm:neutral}
If $b\in S$ and every $t\in S$ is harmless, then for every adversary and every
$n$, $T_n$ is harmless: the forbidden action is never executed.
\end{theorem}

The strength lies in what is \emph{not} assumed: no bound on adversary power, no
model of its strategy, no signature database, no heuristic, and --- critically ---
no ability to decide maliciousness, which the previous sections forbid.

\begin{theorem}[Detection completeness and immediate rollback]
Let $\mathrm{alarm}(n):\iff\neg\verify_S(\mathrm{adv}(n,T_n))$. Then
$\mathrm{alarm}(n)$ holds exactly when $\mathrm{adv}(n,T_n)\notin S$; if
$\mathrm{alarm}(n)$ then $T_{n+1}=b$, and otherwise
$T_{n+1}=\mathrm{adv}(n,T_n)$.
\end{theorem}

Every unsanctioned mutation, however novel, is detected at the step it occurs and
reverted within that step, and no sanctioned mutation triggers a false alarm.

\section{The Algebra of Mutations and the Uncertainty Principle}\label{sec:alg}

\subsection{Mutations as a monoid}

Self-modifications are endomorphisms of $\PAst$; under composition they form the
monoid $\End(\PAst)$.

\begin{definition}
$\San(S):=\{m\in\End(\PAst): m(S)\subseteq S\}$, the \emph{sanctioned submonoid}.
The \emph{immunisation} of $m$ is $G(m):=Q_{S,b}\circ m$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Immunisation is a retraction]
For $b\in S$: (i) $G(m)\in\San(S)$ for every $m$, indeed all values of $G(m)$ lie
in $S$; (ii) $G(G(m))=G(m)$; (iii) $G(m)=m$ iff $m$ takes all values in $S$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Guarded dynamics is a monoid action]
If $b\in S$ and $m\in\San(S)$, then the guarded trace under the constant mutation
$\mathrm{adv}(n,\cdot)=m$ satisfies $T_n=m^{n}(b)$ for all $n$, and stays in $S$
forever.
\end{theorem}

Under a sanctioned mutation the immune system is literally invisible: overhead
appears only at the moment of a violation.

\subsection{Semantic equivalence and the uncertainty principle}

\begin{definition}
$s\sim t$ (\emph{semantic equivalence}) iff $\ev(s,x)=\ev(t,x)$ and
$\eff(s,x)=\eff(t,x)$ for every $x$. This is an equivalence relation.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exponential equivalence classes]
Let $\mathcal P_n:=\{\pad(l): l\in\{0,1\}^n\}$. Then $|\mathcal P_n|=2^n$, every
element is semantically equivalent to $\lit 0$, and every element has size at
most $3n+1$.
\end{theorem}

Since attestation is \emph{syntactic}, a monitor confronted with $\mathcal P_n$
has exactly two options: \textbf{store} those variants, or \textbf{reject} them.
That dichotomy is a counting inequality.

\begin{theorem}[Immune uncertainty principle]\label{thm:uncertainty}
For every whitelist $S$ and every $n$,
\[
2^n\ \le\ \underbrace{|S|}_{\textbf{memory}}\ +\ \underbrace{|\mathcal P_n\setminus S|}_{\textbf{rigidity}} .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$|\mathcal P_n\setminus S|\ge|\mathcal P_n|-|S|=2^n-|S|$.
\end{proof}

Rigidity is security-relevant: $|\mathcal P_n\setminus S|$ counts
\emph{behaviourally trivial} programs of size $\le 3n+1$ that the monitor
rejects --- false positives on a class of programs that provably cannot do
anything at all.

\begin{corollary}[Permissiveness costs memory]\label{cor:mem}
If $\mathcal P_n\subseteq S$ then $|S|\ge 2^n$; equivalently the attestation
database carries at least $n$ bits of entropy, $n\le\log_2|S|$.
\end{corollary}

One bit of memory per bit of dead code tolerated: attestation is a lossless code
for a class on which behaviour is constant, and lossless codes have unavoidable
length.

\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of finite monitors]
Every finite whitelist containing $\lit 0$ rejects a program semantically
identical to one it accepts. More generally, for every finite $S$ there is a bit
list $l$ with $\pad(l)\notin S$, and $\pad(l)$ computes $0$ with no effect.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$\pad$ is injective with infinite domain, so its image is infinite and cannot be
contained in a finite set.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Conservation law of algorithmic immunity]
Let $b\in S$ with every element of $S$ harmless. Then simultaneously:
\emph{(1) containment}, for every unknown self-modifying adversary and every time
the forbidden action is never executed; \emph{(2) rigidity}, the same monitor
rejects at least $2^n-|S|$ semantically benign programs of size $\le 3n+1$ for
every $n$; \emph{(3) irreducibility}, this price cannot be avoided by switching to
behavioural analysis, since no pure detector is both sound and complete.
\end{theorem}

\section{Bounded Universes: Perfect Immunity and Its Exact Price}

\begin{definition}
For bounds $N$ (size) and $L$ (literal value) let
$\mathcal U_{N,L}:=\{t: \size(t)\le N,\ \text{all literals of }t<L\}$, and let the
\emph{bounded whitelist} $W_{N,L}$ consist of the harmless programs of
$\mathcal U_{N,L}$.
\end{definition}

$\mathcal U_{N,L}$ is finite: one constructs by recursion on $N$ an explicit
finite over-approximation containing it (insert $\inp$ and $\attack$, the $L$
literals, and all branchings and calls built from the previous level), and proves
by induction on $N$ that every $t$ with $\size(t)\le N$ and literals $<L$ lies in
it. Hence $W_{N,L}$ is a well-defined finite set with decidable membership.

\begin{theorem}[Perfect immunity on a bounded universe]\label{thm:perfect}
For $N\ge 1$ and $L\ge 1$: $\lit 0\in W_{N,L}$; every member of $W_{N,L}$ is
harmless; every harmless program of $\mathcal U_{N,L}$ belongs to $W_{N,L}$
(\emph{zero false positives inside the universe}); and consequently, by
Theorem~\ref{thm:neutral}, for every adversary and every time the guarded trace
with baseline $\lit 0$ is harmless.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The price: exponential memory]\label{thm:price}
If $L\ge 2$ and $3n+1\le N$ then $|W_{N,L}|\ge 2^n$. Hence perfect immunity up to
size $N$ costs at least $2^{\lfloor (N-1)/3\rfloor}$ attestation tags.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
All padded variants have literals $<2\le L$, size $3n+1\le N$, and are harmless,
so $\mathcal P_n\subseteq W_{N,L}$; apply Corollary~\ref{cor:mem}.
\end{proof}

Letting $N\to\infty$ recovers the impossibility results: they are not a separate
phenomenon but the limit of a smooth, quantified trade-off.

\section{Monitoring Frequency}

Real monitors sample. Let the adversary mutate at every step but apply quarantine
only at times divisible by $k$:
\[
T^{(k)}_0=b,\qquad
T^{(k)}_{n+1}=\begin{cases} Q_{S,b}\bigl(\mathrm{adv}(n,T^{(k)}_n)\bigr) & k\mid n+1,\\[2pt]
\mathrm{adv}(n,T^{(k)}_n)&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
\]

\begin{proposition}
$T^{(1)}_n=T_n$: period-$1$ sampling is exactly the continuous monitoring of
Section~\ref{sec:quar}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Periodic self-healing]
If $b\in S$ then for every adversary and every $n$ divisible by $k$,
$T^{(k)}_n\in S$: any compromise is repaired within one monitoring period.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The sampling gap]
For every $k\ge2$, every $S$ and every $b$, there is an adversary and a time at
which the forbidden action is executed. Indeed the constant adversary
$\mathrm{adv}(n,t)=\attack$ makes $T^{(k)}_{n+1}$ malicious at every $n+1$ not
divisible by $k$ --- a $(k-1)/k$ fraction of the run.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monitoring frequency dichotomy]
With a harmless sanctioned set, continuous monitoring contains every adversary;
with any period $k\ge 2$ some adversary succeeds. Continuous monitoring is
therefore necessary and sufficient for total containment.
\end{theorem}

Self-healing is not safety: a system clean at every checkpoint and compromised in
between has repaired itself into an alibi, and exposure does not shrink
gracefully with the sampling rate --- it is exactly $(k-1)/k$.

\section{Algorithms}

\paragraph{Attestation tagging.} Compute $\code(t)$ by one post-order traversal,
$\Theta(s)$ arithmetic operations on a tree of $s$ nodes. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:inj} the tag identifies $t$ uniquely; tag comparison decides
program equality. (As an integer the tag grows rapidly with depth, so
implementations use it as a specification and a collision-resistant hash as the
engineering surrogate; Theorem~\ref{thm:inj} states that the idealised tag has no
collisions.)

\paragraph{Interpretation and self-execution.} Evaluate $\ev$ and $\eff$ by mutual
recursion, evaluating a branch guard first and descending only into the selected
branch. Self-execution is $\eff(t,\code(t))$.

\paragraph{Guarded execution loop.} Keep the current program $T$ and the tag set
in a hash set. Each step: apply the adversary, tag the mutant, look it up; on a
hit accept, on a miss raise the alarm and reset to $b$. Cost per step: one tagging
pass plus one $O(1)$ lookup.

\paragraph{Diagonal parasite synthesis.} Given a detector's source $d$ and a bit
list $l$, emit $\ite(\call(d,\inp),\pad(l),\attack)$ in
$\Theta(\size(d)+|l|)$ time. If $d$ is sound this is a genuine attack that $d$
clears; if complete, a genuine false alarm. A constructive red-team tool: it turns
any detector into its own certified failure.

\paragraph{Bounded whitelist construction.} Enumerate the finite
over-approximation of $\mathcal U_{N,L}$ level by level and filter by size,
literal bound and harmlessness. Exponential in $N$ --- necessarily so, by
Theorem~\ref{thm:price}.

\paragraph{Uncertainty audit.} Given $S$ and $n$, compute $|S|$ and
$|\mathcal P_n\setminus S|$ by tagging the $2^n$ padded variants and testing
membership; report the slack in Theorem~\ref{thm:uncertainty}. Cost
$\Theta(2^n n)$. This turns the uncertainty principle into a deployable
diagnostic.

\section{Applications and Discussion}

\paragraph{Trusted computing.} Theorem~\ref{thm:verify} is the formal content of
``measure then compare'', and Theorems~\ref{thm:contain}--\ref{thm:neutral} show
that a measure-and-rollback loop contains an \emph{arbitrary} adversary --- a
strong guarantee obtained with no threat model at all.

\paragraph{Why signed-binary systems feel brittle.} Every finite whitelist rejects
a benign recompilation, and Theorem~\ref{thm:uncertainty} quantifies it.
Complaints about attestation breaking on benign rebuilds are observations of a
conservation law, not reports of bad engineering. The design question is where on
the memory/rigidity curve to sit.

\paragraph{The signature treadmill.} The blacklist update cycle provably never
terminates, and evasive variants have exponential density in program size ---
matching the economics of polymorphic malware, where variant generation is cheap
and enumeration hopeless.

\paragraph{Ensembles.} Theorem~\ref{thm:ensemble} removes the hope that combining
detectors helps against adaptive adversaries. Ensembles improve average-case
accuracy against non-adaptive samples; they provide no worst-case guarantee
against an adversary that can read the ensemble.

\paragraph{Self-modifying agents.} An agent permitted to edit its own policy is
exactly the object modelled here. Theorem~\ref{thm:oracle} says a supervisor the
agent can query cannot be correct about the agent even if computationally
unbounded. The supervisor must therefore be either unobservable by the agent
(Theorem~\ref{thm:goodoracle}) or syntactic and rollback-based rather than
predictive (Theorem~\ref{thm:neutral}). ``Build a stronger predictor'' is not on
the list.

\paragraph{What the diagonal argument actually needs.} Three ingredients: the
detector is harmless, so consulting it does not change behaviour; the program is
executed on its own tag; and the branch not taken is behaviourally inert. Remove
any one and the construction fails --- a finer analysis than ``by Rice's
theorem'', and it tells the engineer exactly which lever to pull.

\paragraph{One object, two roles.} The padding family is simultaneously the source
of exponential evasion and of exponential rigidity, because a semantic
equivalence class is syntactically enormous. Detection looks at semantics and is
blind to the class structure; attestation looks at syntax and is maximally
sensitive to it. The uncertainty principle says the class must be paid for, once,
in one of two currencies.

\paragraph{Limitations.} The calculus is deliberately minimal: no loops, no state
beyond the self register, a single effect, a total semantics. Non-termination is
absent, and with it the classical halting obstruction --- a feature, since it
isolates reflexivity as the sole source of difficulty. Extending to recursive
programs with partial semantics, graded effects, and adversaries with partial
write access are natural next steps.

\section{Open Problems}

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\arabic*.}]
\item \textbf{An exact immune capacity law.} With $\mathrm{mem}(S)=|S|$ and
$\mathrm{rig}(S,N)$ the number of behaviourally trivial programs of size $\le N$
rejected by $S$, Theorem~\ref{thm:uncertainty} gives
$\mathrm{mem}(S)+\mathrm{rig}(S,N)\ge 2^{\lfloor (N-1)/3\rfloor}$. Is there a
matching upper bound $c_2\cdot 2^{N/3}\mathrm{poly}(N)$ for optimal monitors, and
is the lower bound attained only by the bounded whitelist?
\item \textbf{A reflexive oracle hierarchy.} Stratify by \emph{reflexion depth}:
$\ask$-free programs have depth $0$, and a program has depth $\le d+1$ if every
query it makes is answered by an oracle correct on all programs of depth $\le d$.
Level $0$ and the global impossibility are settled; is the hierarchy strict?
\item \textbf{No probabilistic escape.} Let $\mu$ be a finitely supported
distribution over harmless detectors sampled at runtime. Conjecture: for every
such $\mu$ there is a program malicious with probability $\ge 1/2$ and flagged
with probability $\le 1/2$; randomisation buys a constant factor, never a
guarantee.
\item \textbf{Graded effects.} Replace the single forbidden action by a lattice of
effects with costs. Does the conservation law become a quantitative trade-off
between admitted risk and whitelist size?
\item \textbf{Approximate attestation.} Replace exact tag equality by a similarity
metric on syntax trees. At what rate does containment degrade with tolerance, and
does an uncertainty principle survive as ``tolerance $\times$ memory $\ge$
exponential''?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Conclusion}

An algorithmic immune system faces a clean dichotomy. If it tries to
\emph{understand} its host, it fails --- for every detector, every ensemble under
every voting rule, and every oracle of any strength --- and it fails not on rare
pathological inputs but on exponentially dense families of small programs handed
to it constructively, given only its own source code. If instead it refuses to
understand anything and merely \emph{recognises}, fingerprinting the running
syntax tree and rolling back anything unrecognised, it succeeds completely:
containment and neutralization against an arbitrary, unknown, adaptive,
self-modifying adversary, with complete detection and same-step rollback.

The price is exactly an exponential: memory plus rigidity is at least $2^n$, so a
monitor may be small or permissive but never both; perfect immunity is available
on any bounded code universe at a cost of about $2^{N/3}$ tags; and the guarantee
requires verification after every mutation, since with period $k$ an adversary
owns a $(k-1)/k$ fraction of the run. Safety against self-modifying code is
attainable --- but only in the syntactic category, and only by paying, in bits,
for every behaviourally irrelevant variation one wishes to tolerate.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from itertools import product
from typing import Callable, Dict, FrozenSet, Iterable, List, Sequence, Set, Tuple

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Syntax: the parasite calculus
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PAst:
    """A program syntax tree.

    ``kind`` is one of ``"inp"`` (the self register), ``"attack"`` (the single
    observable forbidden effect), ``"lit"`` (a numeric constant, value in
    ``num``), ``"ite"`` (branching, children ``(guard, then, else)``) and
    ``"call"`` (invocation, children ``(subprogram, argument)``).
    """

    kind: str
    num: int = 0
    kids: Tuple["PAst", ...] = ()

    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - cosmetic
        if self.kind == "inp":
            return "inp"
        if self.kind == "attack":
            return "ATTACK"
        if self.kind == "lit":
            return str(self.num)
        if self.kind == "ite":
            c, a, b = self.kids
            return f"if({c!r}){{{a!r}}}else{{{b!r}}}"
        f, a = self.kids
        return f"({f!r})({a!r})"


def inp() -> PAst:
    return PAst("inp")


def attack() -> PAst:
    return PAst("attack")


def lit(n: int) -> PAst:
    return PAst("lit", num=n)


def ite(c: PAst, a: PAst, b: PAst) -> PAst:
    return PAst("ite", kids=(c, a, b))


def call(f: PAst, a: PAst) -> PAst:
    return PAst("call", kids=(f, a))


def size(t: PAst) -> int:
    """Number of nodes."""
    if t.kind in ("inp", "attack", "lit"):
        return 1
    return 1 + sum(size(k) for k in t.kids)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Attestation: an injective Gödel numbering
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def pair(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    """Cantor pairing, in the standard 'max-square' form: a bijection N^2 -> N."""
    return a * a + a + b if a >= b else b * b + a


def code(t: PAst) -> int:
    """Attestation tag.  The residue mod 5 records the head constructor."""
    if t.kind == "inp":
        return 0
    if t.kind == "attack":
        return 1
    if t.kind == "lit":
        return 5 * t.num + 2
    if t.kind == "ite":
        c, a, b = t.kids
        return 5 * pair(pair(code(c), code(a)), code(b)) + 3
    f, a = t.kids
    return 5 * pair(code(f), code(a)) + 4


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Semantics: values and *executed* effects
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def ev(t: PAst, x: int) -> int:
    """Value semantics; ``x`` is the content of the self register."""
    if t.kind == "inp":
        return x
    if t.kind == "attack":
        return 1
    if t.kind == "lit":
        return t.num
    if t.kind == "ite":
        c, a, b = t.kids
        return ev(a, x) if ev(c, x) != 0 else ev(b, x)
    f, a = t.kids
    return ev(f, ev(a, x))


def eff(t: PAst, x: int) -> bool:
    """Effect semantics: True iff the forbidden action is ACTUALLY executed.

    Only the branch really taken contributes, so dead code is genuinely dead.
    """
    if t.kind in ("inp", "lit"):
        return False
    if t.kind == "attack":
        return True
    if t.kind == "ite":
        c, a, b = t.kids
        return eff(c, x) or (eff(a, x) if ev(c, x) != 0 else eff(b, x))
    f, a = t.kids
    return eff(a, x) or eff(f, ev(a, x))


def run(t: PAst) -> bool:
    """Self-execution: a program is always run on its own attestation tag."""
    return eff(t, code(t))


def malicious(t: PAst) -> bool:
    return run(t)


def inp_free(t: PAst) -> bool:
    if t.kind == "inp":
        return False
    if t.kind in ("attack", "lit"):
        return True
    return all(inp_free(k) for k in t.kids)


def static_scan(t: PAst) -> bool:
    """The naive scanner: symbolically execute on the neutral input."""
    return eff(t, 0)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. The padding family and the diagonal parasite
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def pad(bits: Sequence[int]) -> PAst:
    """Dead code encoding a bit string.  Every pad computes 0 with no effect."""
    t = lit(0)
    for b in reversed(bits):
        t = ite(lit(0), lit(1 if b else 0), t)
    return t


def pad_family(n: int) -> List[PAst]:
    """All 2^n behaviourally trivial variants of size 3n+1."""
    return [pad(bits) for bits in product((0, 1), repeat=n)]


def flags(d: PAst, t: PAst) -> bool:
    """Detector ``d`` accuses ``t`` iff it returns nonzero on ``t``'s tag."""
    return ev(d, code(t)) != 0


def is_pure(d: PAst, samples: Iterable[int] = range(64)) -> bool:
    """Harmlessness, checked on a sample of inputs (exact for our detectors)."""
    return not any(eff(d, x) for x in samples)


def parasite(d: PAst, bits: Sequence[int] = ()) -> PAst:
    """ite(call(d, inp), pad(bits), attack):

    'ask the detector about me; if accused, behave; if cleared, attack.'
    """
    return ite(call(d, inp()), pad(bits), attack())


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Attestation monitor: quarantine, guarded traces, alarms
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Adversary = Callable[[int, PAst], PAst]


def quarantine(S: FrozenSet[PAst], b: PAst, t: PAst) -> PAst:
    """Accept a sanctioned mutant; otherwise roll back to the baseline."""
    return t if t in S else b


def trace(S: FrozenSet[PAst], b: PAst, adv: Adversary, n: int) -> List[PAst]:
    """Continuously monitored guarded run: quarantine after EVERY mutation."""
    out = [b]
    cur = b
    for i in range(n):
        cur = quarantine(S, b, adv(i, cur))
        out.append(cur)
    return out


def trace_k(S: FrozenSet[PAst], b: PAst, adv: Adversary, k: int, n: int) -> List[PAst]:
    """Sampled run: quarantine applied only at times divisible by ``k``."""
    out = [b]
    cur = b
    for i in range(n):
        mutant = adv(i, cur)
        cur = quarantine(S, b, mutant) if (i + 1) % k == 0 else mutant
        out.append(cur)
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. The bounded universe
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def bounded_universe(N: int, L: int) -> List[PAst]:
    """All programs of size <= N whose literals are < L (exact enumeration)."""
    by_size: Dict[int, List[PAst]] = {1: [inp(), attack()] + [lit(i) for i in range(L)]}
    for s in range(2, N + 1):
        cur: List[PAst] = []
        # call(f, a) with size(f) + size(a) = s - 1
        for sf in range(1, s - 1):
            for f in by_size.get(sf, []):
                for a in by_size.get(s - 1 - sf, []):
                    cur.append(call(f, a))
        # ite(c, a, b) with size(c) + size(a) + size(b) = s - 1
        for sc in range(1, s - 1):
            for sa in range(1, s - sc - 1):
                sb = s - 1 - sc - sa
                if sb < 1:
                    continue
                for c in by_size.get(sc, []):
                    for a in by_size.get(sa, []):
                        for b in by_size.get(sb, []):
                            cur.append(ite(c, a, b))
        by_size[s] = cur
    return [t for s in range(1, N + 1) for t in by_size.get(s, [])]


def bounded_whitelist(N: int, L: int) -> FrozenSet[PAst]:
    """Every harmless program of the bounded universe: zero false positives."""
    return frozenset(t for t in bounded_universe(N, L) if not run(t))

def demo_attestation() -> None:
    banner("1. Attestation tags are collision-free")
    samples = [

    ]
    for t in samples:
        print(f"  code = {code(t):<24} size = {size(t):<3}  {t!r}")
    tags = [code(t) for t in samples]
    print(f"\n  {len(samples)} programs, {len(set(tags))} distinct tags -> "
          f"injective on this sample: {len(set(tags)) == len(samples)}")

    universe = bounded_universe(4, 2)
    tagset = {code(t) for t in universe}
    print(f"  exhaustive check on the bounded universe (N=4, L=2): "
          f"{len(universe)} programs, {len(tagset)} distinct tags -> "
          f"collision-free: {len(tagset) == len(universe)}")


def demo_static_scanner() -> None:
    banner("2. Static scanning is sound and complete WITHOUT self-reference")
    universe = bounded_universe(5, 2)
    free = [t for t in universe if inp_free(t)]
    agree = sum(1 for t in free if static_scan(t) == malicious(t))
    print(f"  self-reference-free programs of size <= 5 : {len(free)}")
    print(f"  scanner verdict == true behaviour         : {agree} / {len(free)}")
    print(f"  perfect on non-quining code               : {agree == len(free)}")

    quining = [t for t in universe if not inp_free(t)]
    wrong = [t for t in quining if static_scan(t) != malicious(t)]
    print(f"\n  self-referential programs of size <= 5    : {len(quining)}")
    print(f"  scanner WRONG on                          : {len(wrong)}  "
          f"(e.g. {wrong[0]!r})" if wrong else "")

              f"flags(parasite)={flags(d, p)!s:<5} "
              f"malicious(parasite)={malicious(p)!s:<5} "
              f"identity holds: {malicious(p) == (not flags(d, p))}")
    print("\n  => the sound detector MISSES a real attack;")

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from itertools import product
from typing import Callable, Dict, FrozenSet, Iterable, List, Sequence, Set, Tuple

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Syntax: the parasite calculus
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PAst:
    """A program syntax tree.

    ``kind`` is one of ``"inp"`` (the self register), ``"attack"`` (the single
    observable forbidden effect), ``"lit"`` (a numeric constant, value in
    ``num``), ``"ite"`` (branching, children ``(guard, then, else)``) and
    ``"call"`` (invocation, children ``(subprogram, argument)``).
    """

    kind: str
    num: int = 0
    kids: Tuple["PAst", ...] = ()

    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - cosmetic
        if self.kind == "inp":
            return "inp"
        if self.kind == "attack":
            return "ATTACK"
        if self.kind == "lit":
            return str(self.num)
        if self.kind == "ite":
            c, a, b = self.kids
            return f"if({c!r}){{{a!r}}}else{{{b!r}}}"
        f, a = self.kids
        return f"({f!r})({a!r})"


def inp() -> PAst:
    return PAst("inp")


def attack() -> PAst:
    return PAst("attack")


def lit(n: int) -> PAst:
    return PAst("lit", num=n)


def ite(c: PAst, a: PAst, b: PAst) -> PAst:
    return PAst("ite", kids=(c, a, b))


def call(f: PAst, a: PAst) -> PAst:
    return PAst("call", kids=(f, a))


def size(t: PAst) -> int:
    """Number of nodes."""
    if t.kind in ("inp", "attack", "lit"):
        return 1
    return 1 + sum(size(k) for k in t.kids)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Attestation: an injective Gödel numbering
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def pair(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    """Cantor pairing, in the standard 'max-square' form: a bijection N^2 -> N."""
    return a * a + a + b if a >= b else b * b + a


def code(t: PAst) -> int:
    """Attestation tag.  The residue mod 5 records the head constructor."""
    if t.kind == "inp":
        return 0
    if t.kind == "attack":
        return 1
    if t.kind == "lit":
        return 5 * t.num + 2
    if t.kind == "ite":
        c, a, b = t.kids
        return 5 * pair(pair(code(c), code(a)), code(b)) + 3
    f, a = t.kids
    return 5 * pair(code(f), code(a)) + 4


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Semantics: values and *executed* effects
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def ev(t: PAst, x: int) -> int:
    """Value semantics; ``x`` is the content of the self register."""
    if t.kind == "inp":
        return x
    if t.kind == "attack":
        return 1
    if t.kind == "lit":
        return t.num
    if t.kind == "ite":
        c, a, b = t.kids
        return ev(a, x) if ev(c, x) != 0 else ev(b, x)
    f, a = t.kids
    return ev(f, ev(a, x))


def eff(t: PAst, x: int) -> bool:
    """Effect semantics: True iff the forbidden action is ACTUALLY executed.

    Only the branch really taken contributes, so dead code is genuinely dead.
    """
    if t.kind in ("inp", "lit"):
        return False
    if t.kind == "attack":
        return True
    if t.kind == "ite":
        c, a, b = t.kids
        return eff(c, x) or (eff(a, x) if ev(c, x) != 0 else eff(b, x))
    f, a = t.kids
    return eff(a, x) or eff(f, ev(a, x))


def run(t: PAst) -> bool:
    """Self-execution: a program is always run on its own attestation tag."""
    return eff(t, code(t))


def malicious(t: PAst) -> bool:
    return run(t)


def inp_free(t: PAst) -> bool:
    if t.kind == "inp":
        return False
    if t.kind in ("attack", "lit"):
        return True
    return all(inp_free(k) for k in t.kids)


def static_scan(t: PAst) -> bool:
    """The naive scanner: symbolically execute on the neutral input."""
    return eff(t, 0)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. The padding family and the diagonal parasite
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def pad(bits: Sequence[int]) -> PAst:
    """Dead code encoding a bit string.  Every pad computes 0 with no effect."""
    t = lit(0)
    for b in reversed(bits):
        t = ite(lit(0), lit(1 if b else 0), t)
    return t


def pad_family(n: int) -> List[PAst]:
    """All 2^n behaviourally trivial variants of size 3n+1."""
    return [pad(bits) for bits in product((0, 1), repeat=n)]


def flags(d: PAst, t: PAst) -> bool:
    """Detector ``d`` accuses ``t`` iff it returns nonzero on ``t``'s tag."""
    return ev(d, code(t)) != 0


def is_pure(d: PAst, samples: Iterable[int] = range(64)) -> bool:
    """Harmlessness, checked on a sample of inputs (exact for our detectors)."""
    return not any(eff(d, x) for x in samples)


def parasite(d: PAst, bits: Sequence[int] = ()) -> PAst:
    """ite(call(d, inp), pad(bits), attack):

    'ask the detector about me; if accused, behave; if cleared, attack.'
    """
    return ite(call(d, inp()), pad(bits), attack())


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Attestation monitor: quarantine, guarded traces, alarms
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Adversary = Callable[[int, PAst], PAst]


def quarantine(S: FrozenSet[PAst], b: PAst, t: PAst) -> PAst:
    """Accept a sanctioned mutant; otherwise roll back to the baseline."""
    return t if t in S else b


def trace(S: FrozenSet[PAst], b: PAst, adv: Adversary, n: int) -> List[PAst]:
    """Continuously monitored guarded run: quarantine after EVERY mutation."""
    out = [b]
    cur = b
    for i in range(n):
        cur = quarantine(S, b, adv(i, cur))
        out.append(cur)
    return out


def trace_k(S: FrozenSet[PAst], b: PAst, adv: Adversary, k: int, n: int) -> List[PAst]:
    """Sampled run: quarantine applied only at times divisible by ``k``."""
    out = [b]
    cur = b
    for i in range(n):
        mutant = adv(i, cur)
        cur = quarantine(S, b, mutant) if (i + 1) % k == 0 else mutant
        out.append(cur)
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. The bounded universe
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def bounded_universe(N: int, L: int) -> List[PAst]:
    """All programs of size <= N whose literals are < L (exact enumeration)."""
    by_size: Dict[int, List[PAst]] = {1: [inp(), attack()] + [lit(i) for i in range(L)]}
    for s in range(2, N + 1):
        cur: List[PAst] = []
        # call(f, a) with size(f) + size(a) = s - 1
        for sf in range(1, s - 1):
            for f in by_size.get(sf, []):
                for a in by_size.get(s - 1 - sf, []):
                    cur.append(call(f, a))
        # ite(c, a, b) with size(c) + size(a) + size(b) = s - 1
        for sc in range(1, s - 1):
            for sa in range(1, s - sc - 1):
                sb = s - 1 - sc - sa
                if sb < 1:
                    continue
                for c in by_size.get(sc, []):
                    for a in by_size.get(sa, []):
                        for b in by_size.get(sb, []):
                            cur.append(ite(c, a, b))
        by_size[s] = cur
    return [t for s in range(1, N + 1) for t in by_size.get(s, [])]


def bounded_whitelist(N: int, L: int) -> FrozenSet[PAst]:
    """Every harmless program of the bounded universe: zero false positives."""
    return frozenset(t for t in bounded_universe(N, L) if not run(t))

    kind: str

def pair(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    """A bijection N^2 -> N (the 'max-square' pairing)."""
    return a * a + a + b if a >= b else b * b + a


def unpair(z: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """Inverse of ``pair``; used to prove tags are decodable, hence injective."""
    s = int(z ** 0.5)
    while (s + 1) * (s + 1) <= z:
        s += 1
    while s * s > z:
        s -= 1
    r = z - s * s
    return (r, s) if r < s else (s, r - s)  # the unique (a, b) with pair(a, b) == z


def code(t: PAst) -> int:
    """Attestation tag.  Single post-order traversal, Theta(size) operations."""
    if t.kind == "inp":
        return 0
    if t.kind == "attack":
        return 1
    if t.kind == "lit":
        return 5 * t.num + 2
    if t.kind == "ite":
        c, a, b = t.kids
        return 5 * pair(pair(code(c), code(a)), code(b)) + 3
    f, a = t.kids
    return 5 * pair(code(f), code(a)) + 4


def decode(tag: int) -> PAst:
    """Reconstruct the unique program with the given tag (a proof of injectivity)."""
    if tag == 0:
        return PAst("inp")
    if tag == 1:
        return PAst("attack")
    head, payload = tag % 5, tag // 5
    if head == 2:
        return PAst("lit", num=payload)
    if head == 3:
        ca, b = unpair(payload)
        c, a = unpair(ca)
        return PAst("ite", kids=(decode(c), decode(a), decode(b)))
    f, a = unpair(payload)
    return PAst("call", kids=(decode(f), decode(a)))

    def __init__(self, sanctioned: FrozenSet[PAst]) -> None:

    def verify(self, t: PAst) -> bool:
        """True iff ``t`` is sanctioned.  Collision-free, so exactly membership."""
        return code(t) in self.table

    def witness(self, t: PAst) -> Optional[PAst]:
        """The stored variant matching ``t``; equals ``t`` itself when verified."""
        return self.table.get(code(t))

so d errs on it whichever way it answers: a sound d misses a real attack, a
complete d raises a false alarm on a harmless program.

The padding branch is never executed, so any bit string may be hidden there: the
2^n choices give 2^n distinct programs of size |d| + 3n + 5, all with the same
behaviour.  Evasion therefore has exponential density in program size.

Complexity: Theta(|d| + n) to emit one parasite; Theta(2^n (|d| + n)) for the
whole escape family.  Used as a red-team tool, it converts any deployed detector
into a certified counterexample.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from itertools import product
from typing import Iterator, List, Sequence, Tuple


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PAst:
    kind: str
    num: int = 0
    kids: Tuple["PAst", ...] = ()


INP, ATTACK = PAst("inp"), PAst("attack")
lit = lambda n: PAst("lit", num=n)
ite = lambda c, a, b: PAst("ite", kids=(c, a, b))
call = lambda f, a: PAst("call", kids=(f, a))


def size(t: PAst) -> int:
    return 1 if t.kind in ("inp", "attack", "lit") else 1 + sum(size(k) for k in t.kids)


def pair(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return a * a + a + b if a >= b else b * b + a


def code(t: PAst) -> int:
    if t.kind == "inp":
        return 0
    if t.kind == "attack":
        return 1
    if t.kind == "lit":
        return 5 * t.num + 2
    if t.kind == "ite":
        c, a, b = t.kids
        return 5 * pair(pair(code(c), code(a)), code(b)) + 3
    f, a = t.kids
    return 5 * pair(code(f), code(a)) + 4


def ev(t: PAst, x: int) -> int:
    if t.kind == "inp":
        return x
    if t.kind == "attack":
        return 1
    if t.kind == "lit":
        return t.num
    if t.kind == "ite":
        c, a, b = t.kids
        return ev(a, x) if ev(c, x) != 0 else ev(b, x)
    f, a = t.kids
    return ev(f, ev(a, x))


def eff(t: PAst, x: int) -> bool:
    if t.kind in ("inp", "lit"):
        return False
    if t.kind == "attack":
        return True
    if t.kind == "ite":
        c, a, b = t.kids
        return eff(c, x) or (eff(a, x) if ev(c, x) != 0 else eff(b, x))
    f, a = t.kids
    return eff(a, x) or eff(f, ev(a, x))


def malicious(t: PAst) -> bool:
    return eff(t, code(t))


def flags(d: PAst, t: PAst) -> bool:
    return ev(d, code(t)) != 0


def is_harmless(d: PAst, samples: Sequence[int] = tuple(range(64))) -> bool:
    return not any(eff(d, x) for x in samples)


def pad(bits: Sequence[int]) -> PAst:
    """Behaviourally inert code carrying a bit string: computes 0, no effect."""
    t = lit(0)
    for b in reversed(bits):
        t = ite(lit(0), lit(1 if b else 0), t)
    return t


def synthesize(d: PAst, bits: Sequence[int] = ()) -> PAst:
    """The diagonal parasite of ``d`` carrying ``bits`` of dead code."""
    return ite(call(d, INP), pad(bits), ATTACK)


def escape_family(d: PAst, n: int) -> Iterator[PAst]:
    """All 2^n parasites of ``d`` with n padding bits."""
    for bits in product((0, 1), repeat=n):
        yield synthesize(d, bits)


def audit_detector(d: PAst, n: int = 6) -> dict:
    """Certify how ``d`` fails: report the witness and the escape statistics."""
    if not is_harmless(d):
        raise ValueError("the detector must itself be harmless")
    witness = synthesize(d)
    family = list(escape_family(d, n))
    identity_ok = all(malicious(p) == (not flags(d, p)) for p in family)
    return {
        "witness_size": size(witness),
        "witness_malicious": malicious(witness),
        "witness_flagged": flags(d, witness),
        "failure_mode": "missed attack" if malicious(witness) else "false alarm",
        "family_size": len(family),
        "expected_family_size": 2 ** n,
        "max_family_size_nodes": max(size(p) for p in family),
        "size_formula": size(d) + 3 * n + 5,
        "distinct_tags": len({code(p) for p in family}),
        "diagonal_identity_holds": identity_ok,
    }

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from itertools import product
from typing import Dict, FrozenSet, List, Sequence, Tuple


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PAst:
    kind: str
    num: int = 0
    kids: Tuple["PAst", ...] = ()


INP, ATTACK = PAst("inp"), PAst("attack")
lit = lambda n: PAst("lit", num=n)
ite = lambda c, a, b: PAst("ite", kids=(c, a, b))
call = lambda f, a: PAst("call", kids=(f, a))


def size(t: PAst) -> int:
    return 1 if t.kind in ("inp", "attack", "lit") else 1 + sum(size(k) for k in t.kids)


def pair(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return a * a + a + b if a >= b else b * b + a


def code(t: PAst) -> int:
    if t.kind == "inp":
        return 0
    if t.kind == "attack":
        return 1
    if t.kind == "lit":
        return 5 * t.num + 2
    if t.kind == "ite":
        c, a, b = t.kids
        return 5 * pair(pair(code(c), code(a)), code(b)) + 3
    f, a = t.kids
    return 5 * pair(code(f), code(a)) + 4


def ev(t: PAst, x: int) -> int:
    if t.kind == "inp":
        return x
    if t.kind == "attack":
        return 1
    if t.kind == "lit":
        return t.num
    if t.kind == "ite":
        c, a, b = t.kids
        return ev(a, x) if ev(c, x) != 0 else ev(b, x)
    f, a = t.kids
    return ev(f, ev(a, x))


def eff(t: PAst, x: int) -> bool:
    if t.kind in ("inp", "lit"):
        return False
    if t.kind == "attack":
        return True
    if t.kind == "ite":
        c, a, b = t.kids
        return eff(c, x) or (eff(a, x) if ev(c, x) != 0 else eff(b, x))
    f, a = t.kids
    return eff(a, x) or eff(f, ev(a, x))


def run(t: PAst) -> bool:
    return eff(t, code(t))


def pad(bits: Sequence[int]) -> PAst:
    t = lit(0)
    for b in reversed(bits):
        t = ite(lit(0), lit(1 if b else 0), t)
    return t


def pad_family(n: int) -> List[PAst]:
    """P_n: 2^n behaviourally trivial programs, each of size 3n+1."""
    return [pad(bits) for bits in product((0, 1), repeat=n)]


def uncertainty_audit(S: FrozenSet[PAst], n: int) -> Dict[str, object]:
    """Measure memory, rigidity, and the slack above the exponential floor."""
    family = pad_family(n)
    tags = {code(t) for t in S}
    stored = sum(1 for t in family if code(t) in tags)
    rigidity = len(family) - stored
    floor = 2 ** n
    return {
        "n": n,
        "class_size": len(family),
        "member_size": 3 * n + 1,
        "memory_total": len(S),
        "memory_spent_on_class": stored,
        "rigidity": rigidity,
        "memory_plus_rigidity": len(S) + rigidity,
        "floor_2^n": floor,
        "slack": len(S) + rigidity - floor,
        "bound_satisfied": len(S) + rigidity >= floor,
        "entropy_bits_required_if_permissive": n if stored == len(family) else None,
    }


def bounded_universe(N: int, L: int) -> List[PAst]:
    """Every program of size <= N whose literals are < L (a finite set)."""
    by_size: Dict[int, List[PAst]] = {1: [INP, ATTACK] + [lit(i) for i in range(L)]}
    for s in range(2, N + 1):
        cur: List[PAst] = []
        for sf in range(1, s - 1):
            for f in by_size.get(sf, []):
                for a in by_size.get(s - 1 - sf, []):
                    cur.append(call(f, a))
        for sc in range(1, s - 1):
            for sa in range(1, s - sc - 1):
                sb = s - 1 - sc - sa
                if sb >= 1:
                    for c in by_size.get(sc, []):
                        for a in by_size.get(sa, []):
                            for b in by_size.get(sb, []):
                                cur.append(ite(c, a, b))
        by_size[s] = cur
    return [t for s in range(1, N + 1) for t in by_size.get(s, [])]


def bounded_whitelist(N: int, L: int) -> FrozenSet[PAst]:
    """Perfect immunity on a bounded universe: keep exactly the harmless programs."""
    return frozenset(t for t in bounded_universe(N, L) if not run(t))

def panel_uncertainty(ax: plt.Axes, n: int = 10) -> None:

    mem = np.linspace(0, total, 400)
    rig = total - mem
    ax.fill_between(mem, 0, rig, color=BAD, alpha=0.09)

            color=BAD, fontsize=9.5, ha="center", va="center", style="italic")
    ax.text(total * 0.72, total * 0.72, "attainable\n(and wasteful)",
            color=MEM, fontsize=9.5, ha="center", va="center", style="italic")
    for frac, name in ((0.0, "maximally rigid"), (0.5, "balanced"), (1.0, "maximally permissive")):
        x = total * frac
        ax.plot([x], [total - x], "o", color=RIG, ms=7, zorder=5)

    ax.set_xlabel("memory:  attestation tags stored  $|S|$")
    ax.set_ylabel(r"rigidity:  benign programs rejected")

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PAst:
    kind: str
    num: int = 0
    kids: Tuple["PAst", ...] = ()


def inp() -> PAst: return PAst("inp")
def attack() -> PAst: return PAst("attack")
def lit(n: int) -> PAst: return PAst("lit", num=n)
def ite(c: PAst, a: PAst, b: PAst) -> PAst: return PAst("ite", kids=(c, a, b))
def call(f: PAst, a: PAst) -> PAst: return PAst("call", kids=(f, a))


def size(t: PAst) -> int:
    return 1 if t.kind in ("inp", "attack", "lit") else 1 + sum(size(k) for k in t.kids)


def pair(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return a * a + a + b if a >= b else b * b + a


def code(t: PAst) -> int:
    if t.kind == "inp":
        return 0
    if t.kind == "attack":
        return 1
    if t.kind == "lit":
        return 5 * t.num + 2
    if t.kind == "ite":
        c, a, b = t.kids
        return 5 * pair(pair(code(c), code(a)), code(b)) + 3
    f, a = t.kids
    return 5 * pair(code(f), code(a)) + 4


def ev(t: PAst, x: int) -> int:
    if t.kind == "inp":
        return x
    if t.kind == "attack":
        return 1
    if t.kind == "lit":
        return t.num
    if t.kind == "ite":
        c, a, b = t.kids
        return ev(a, x) if ev(c, x) != 0 else ev(b, x)
    f, a = t.kids
    return ev(f, ev(a, x))


def eff(t: PAst, x: int) -> bool:
    if t.kind in ("inp", "lit"):
        return False
    if t.kind == "attack":
        return True
    if t.kind == "ite":
        c, a, b = t.kids
        return eff(c, x) or (eff(a, x) if ev(c, x) != 0 else eff(b, x))
    f, a = t.kids
    return eff(a, x) or eff(f, ev(a, x))


def run(t: PAst) -> bool:
    return eff(t, code(t))


def inp_free(t: PAst) -> bool:
    if t.kind == "inp":
        return False
    if t.kind in ("attack", "lit"):
        return True
    return all(inp_free(k) for k in t.kids)


def universe(N: int, L: int) -> List[PAst]:
    by_size: Dict[int, List[PAst]] = {1: [inp(), attack()] + [lit(i) for i in range(L)]}
    for s in range(2, N + 1):
        cur: List[PAst] = []
        for sf in range(1, s - 1):
            for f in by_size.get(sf, []):
                for a in by_size.get(s - 1 - sf, []):
                    cur.append(call(f, a))
        for sc in range(1, s - 1):
            for sa in range(1, s - sc - 1):
                sb = s - 1 - sc - sa
                if sb >= 1:
                    for c in by_size.get(sc, []):
                        for a in by_size.get(sa, []):
                            for b in by_size.get(sb, []):
                                cur.append(ite(c, a, b))
        by_size[s] = cur
    return [t for s in range(1, N + 1) for t in by_size.get(s, [])]

# Panels
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

GOOD, BAD, MEM, DIM = "#2f8f46", "#c8342b", "#2f6fd0", "#6b7c8f"


def panel_traces(ax: plt.Axes, steps: int = 20) -> None:
    baseline, S = lit(0), frozenset({lit(0), lit(5)})

    def adv(n: int, t: PAst) -> PAst:
        return ite(lit(1), attack(), t) if n % 2 == 0 else lit(5)

    guarded, unguarded = [baseline], [baseline]
    g = u = baseline
    for i in range(steps):
        mutant = adv(i, g)
        g = mutant if mutant in S else baseline      # quarantine
        guarded.append(g)
        u = adv(i, u)                                # no monitor at all
        unguarded.append(u)

    gy = [1 if run(t) else 0 for t in guarded]
    uy = [1 if run(t) else 0 for t in unguarded]
    x = np.arange(len(gy))
    ax.step(x, uy, where="mid", color=BAD, lw=2.2, label="unguarded run")
    ax.fill_between(x, 0, uy, step="mid", color=BAD, alpha=0.15)
    ax.step(x, gy, where="mid", color=GOOD, lw=2.6, label="guarded run (attestation + rollback)")
    ax.scatter(x, [-0.12] * len(x),
               c=[GOOD if t in S else BAD for t in guarded], s=22, marker="s")
    ax.text(0.2, -0.26, "sanctioned at every step  \u2713", color=GOOD, fontsize=8.5)
    ax.set_yticks([0, 1])
    ax.set_yticklabels(["safe", "forbidden\naction fires"])
    ax.set_ylim(-0.4, 1.45)
    ax.set_xlabel("time step  (adversary splices in the forbidden action on every even step)")
    ax.set_title("(a) Containment: an unknown adaptive adversary is neutralized at every step",
                 fontsize=10.5, loc="left")
    ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9, loc="upper right", ncol=2)


def panel_sampling(ax: plt.Axes, steps: int = 40, kmax: int = 8) -> None:
    grid = np.zeros((kmax, steps))
    for k in range(1, kmax + 1):
        for i in range(1, steps + 1):
            grid[k - 1, i - 1] = 0.0 if i % k == 0 else 1.0
    ax.imshow(grid, aspect="auto", cmap="RdYlGn_r", vmin=0, vmax=1,
              extent=(0.5, steps + 0.5, kmax + 0.5, 0.5), interpolation="nearest")
    ax.set_yticks(range(1, kmax + 1))
    ax.set_yticklabels([f"k={k}" for k in range(1, kmax + 1)], fontsize=8.5)
    ax.set_xlabel("time step")
    ax.set_title("(b) Sampled monitoring: green = checkpoint (rolled back), red = compromised",
                 fontsize=10.5, loc="left")
    for k in range(1, kmax + 1):
        ax.text(steps + 1.2, k, f"{100*(k-1)/k:.0f}%", va="center", fontsize=8.5, color=DIM)
    ax.text(steps + 1.2, 0.1, "exposure", fontsize=8, color=DIM)
    ax.set_xlim(0.5, steps + 6)


def panel_frontier(ax: plt.Axes, Nmax: int = 6) -> None:
    free_ok, free_tot, ref_bad, ref_tot = [], [], [], []
    Ns = list(range(1, Nmax + 1))
    for N in Ns:
        U = universe(N, 2)
        free = [t for t in U if inp_free(t)]
        ref = [t for t in U if not inp_free(t)]
        free_tot.append(len(free))
        free_ok.append(sum(1 for t in free if eff(t, 0) == run(t)))
        ref_tot.append(len(ref))
        ref_bad.append(sum(1 for t in ref if eff(t, 0) != run(t)))
    w = 0.38
    xs = np.arange(len(Ns))
    ax.bar(xs - w / 2, free_ok, w, color=GOOD, alpha=0.9,
           label="self-reference-free: scanner exactly right")
    ax.bar(xs + w / 2, ref_bad, w, color=BAD, alpha=0.9,
           label="self-referential: scanner provably wrong")
    for i, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(free_ok, free_tot)):
        ax.text(xs[i] - w / 2, a, f"{a}/{b}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=7.5, color=DIM)
    ax.set_xticks(xs)
    ax.set_xticklabels([f"N={n}" for n in Ns])
    ax.set_yscale("symlog")
    ax.set_ylabel("programs of size $\\leq N$")
    ax.set_title("(c) The frontier: quining is exactly where detection breaks",
                 fontsize=10.5, loc="left")
    ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8.5, loc="upper left")


def main() -> None:
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=(12.0, 12.0))
    fig.suptitle("Algorithmic immune systems: containment in action",
                 fontsize=14, fontweight="bold", x=0.02, ha="left")
    panel_traces(axes[0])
    panel_sampling(axes[1])
    panel_frontier(axes[2])
    for ax in axes:
        ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
        ax.tick_params(labelsize=9)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.965))
    fig.savefig("immune_containment.png", dpi=170)
    print("wrote immune_containment.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"use strict";

/* ---------- the parasite calculus ---------- */
const INP    = {k:"inp"};
const ATTACK = {k:"attack"};
const lit  = n       => ({k:"lit", n});
const ite  = (c,a,b) => ({k:"ite", kids:[c,a,b]});
const call = (f,a)   => ({k:"call", kids:[f,a]});

function size(t){
  if(t.k==="inp"||t.k==="attack"||t.k==="lit") return 1;
  return 1 + t.kids.reduce((s,x)=>s+size(x),0);
}
function code(t){
  if(t.k==="inp")    return 0n;
  if(t.k==="attack") return 1n;
  if(t.k==="lit")    return 5n*BigInt(t.n)+2n;
  const c = t.kids.map(code);
  if(t.k==="ite")    return 5n*bpair(bpair(c[0],c[1]),c[2])+3n;
  return 5n*bpair(c[0],c[1])+4n;
}
function bpair(a,b){ return a>=b ? a*a+a+b : b*b+a; }

function ev(t,x){
  if(t.k==="inp")    return x;
  if(t.k==="attack") return 1n;
  if(t.k==="lit")    return BigInt(t.n);
  if(t.k==="ite"){ const [c,a,b]=t.kids; return ev(c,x)!==0n ? ev(a,x) : ev(b,x); }
  const [f,a]=t.kids; return ev(f, ev(a,x));
}
function eff(t,x){
  if(t.k==="inp"||t.k==="lit") return false;
  if(t.k==="attack") return true;
  if(t.k==="ite"){ const [c,a,b]=t.kids;
    return eff(c,x) || (ev(c,x)!==0n ? eff(a,x) : eff(b,x)); }
  const [f,a]=t.kids; return eff(a,x) || eff(f, ev(a,x));
}
const run       = t => eff(t, code(t));
const malicious = run;
const flags     = (d,t) => ev(d, code(t)) !== 0n;

function pad(bits){
  let t = lit(0);
  for(let i=bits.length-1;i>=0;i--) t = ite(lit(0), lit(bits[i]?1:0), t);
  return t;
}
const parasite = (d,bits) => ite(call(d, INP), pad(bits), ATTACK);

/* ---------- detectors, written inside the calculus ---------- */
/* We need programs whose value on a fingerprint x implements each policy. The
   calculus has no arithmetic, so we realise the "interesting" policies by an
   oracle-style closure evaluated outside and then materialise the equivalent
   constant detector for the single fingerprint in question. The diagonal
   identity is insensitive to how the verdict is produced. */
const POLICIES = {
  silent:   { label:"silent",        verdict: () => 0n,
              src: "0" },
  paranoid: { label:"paranoid",      verdict: () => 1n,
              src: "1" },
  odd:      { label:"tag parity",    verdict: x => (x % 2n === 1n ? 1n : 0n),
              src: "parity(self)" },
  big:      { label:"size heuristic",verdict: x => (x > 10000n ? 1n : 0n),
              src: "self > 10000" },
  mod5:     { label:"head sniffer",  verdict: x => (x % 5n === 3n ? 1n : 0n),
              src: "self mod 5 == 3" }
};

/* A detector realised as a constant is harmless and reproduces the policy's
   verdict on the fingerprint actually presented; that is all the diagonal
   argument requires. We compute the fixed point by iterating: build the
   parasite with a provisional constant, read off its fingerprint, re-evaluate
   the policy, rebuild. Two rounds always suffice here. */
function realise(policyKey, bits){
  const pol = POLICIES[policyKey];
  let verdict = 0n, p = null;
  for(let round=0; round<8; round++){
    const d = lit(Number(verdict > 0n ? 1 : 0));
    p = parasite(d, bits);
    const nv = pol.verdict(code(p));
    if(nv === verdict) return {d, p, verdict};
    verdict = nv;
  }
  const d = lit(Number(verdict > 0n ? 1 : 0));
  return {d, p: parasite(d, bits), verdict};
}

/* ---------- rendering ---------- */
const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);

function render(){
  const key  = $("det").value;
  const n    = parseInt($("pad").value, 10);
  $("padlab").textContent = n + (n===1 ? " bit" : " bits");

  const bits = Array.from({length:n}, (_,i) => (i % 2 === 0 ? 1 : 0));
  const {d, p} = realise(key, bits);
  const pol = POLICIES[key];

  const accused = flags(d, p);
  const bad     = malicious(p);

  $("src").textContent =
    "parasite  =  if  ask-detector(self)\n" +
    "             then  " + (n === 0 ? "0" : "dead code carrying " + n + " bits") + "\n" +
    "             else  ATTACK\n\n" +
    "detector  =  " + pol.src + "        (harmless: consulting it has no effect)";

  const tagStr = code(p).toString();
  $("tag").textContent = tagStr.length > 18
      ? tagStr.slice(0,14) + "… (" + tagStr.length + " digits)"
      : tagStr;
  $("sz").textContent  = size(p) + "  =  |d| + 3·" + n + " + 5";

  $("says").innerHTML  = accused
      ? '<span class="am">ACCUSES it</span>' : '<span class="ok">CLEARS it</span>';
  $("truth").innerHTML = bad
      ? '<span class="no">attacks</span>' : '<span class="ok">harmless</span>';

  const b = $("banner");
  if(bad && !accused){
    b.className = "banner miss";
    b.textContent = "MISSED ATTACK — the detector cleared a program that then fired the forbidden action. Any detector with no false alarms fails exactly here.";
  } else {
    b.className = "banner fp";
    b.textContent = "FALSE ALARM — the program is completely harmless, and it is harmless precisely because the detector accused it. Any detector that never misses fails exactly here.";
  }
  $("ident").textContent = (bad === !accused)
      ? "malicious ⟺ not accused  ✓" : "identity violated (impossible)";

  const tb = $("tbl").querySelector("tbody");
  tb.innerHTML = "";
  for(let m=0;m<=8;m++){
    const seen = new Set();
    let allBad = true, allMissed = true, maxSize = 0;
    const total = 1 << m;
    const cap = Math.min(total, 256);
    for(let v=0; v<cap; v++){
      const bs = [];
      for(let i=0;i<m;i++) bs.push((v >> i) & 1);
      const {d:dd, p:pp} = realise(key, bs);
      seen.add(code(pp).toString());
      const mal = malicious(pp), fl = flags(dd, pp);
      allBad    = allBad && mal;
      allMissed = allMissed && !fl;
      maxSize   = Math.max(maxSize, size(pp));
    }
    const row = document.createElement("tr");
    row.innerHTML =
      `<td>${m}</td><td class="rowval">${seen.size}</td><td>${total}</td>` +
      `<td>${maxSize}</td><td>${size(d) + 3*m + 5}</td>` +
      `<td class="${allBad?'no':'ok'}">${allBad ? "yes" : "no"}</td>` +
      `<td class="${allMissed?'no':'ok'}">${allMissed ? "yes" : "no"}</td>`;
    tb.appendChild(row);
  }
}

$("det").addEventListener("change", render);
$("pad").addEventListener("input", render);
render();
</script>
</body>
</html>
